nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Net zero energy buildings_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What are the main objectives of studying traditional residential buildings in the Sichuan Plateau?
nodes.answer: The main objectives are to address limited energy resources and weak infrastructure by optimizing building design, reducing energy waste, and exploring the use of renewable energy sources like local solar energy.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Net zero energy buildings_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is lacking in the research on ethnic minority dwellings in the Sichuan Plateau?
nodes.answer: There is a relative lack of interdisciplinary cooperation and exchange, as well as limited empirical studies on building energy consumption.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Net zero energy buildings_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What approach does Li24 propose to achieve near-zero energy heating in rural residential buildings on the Lhasa plateau?
nodes.answer: Li24 proposes adopting efficient passive design methods to achieve near-zero energy heating in rural residential buildings on the Lhasa plateau.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Net zero energy buildings_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What does the study by Tahmasbi et al. focus on regarding energy-efficient facade designs?
nodes.answer: It explores the latest technologies and strategic approaches that allow facades to respond dynamically to environmental conditions and improve thermal performance for net-zero energy buildings.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Net zero energy buildings_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the main focus of Tahmasbi et al.'s research mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: They focus on the latest technologies and strategic approaches to building energy-efficient facade designs that enable dynamic responses to environmental conditions and improve thermal performance for achieving net-zero energy buildings.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Green buildings|Net zero energy buildings_qna_005
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How much investment per year is estimated to be necessary in the global energy sector to achieve net zero by 2050?
nodes.answer: It is estimated that USD $4.5 trillion per year in global energy sector investment will be necessary to achieve net zero by 2050.
